title: Tell Me Why... AI has killed the author
gist: Prospect podcast episode summary: Alys Key, Alona Ferber and Imaan Irfan discuss AI's impact on literature after recent literary awards became mired in scandal over entries allegedly written by AI. Only a short episode blurb is available, so detail is limited.

insights.claim: Recent literary awards became mired in scandal over entries allegedly written by AI, raising the question of whether it matters who or what wrote a prize-winning story.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Provenance and authenticity disputes in creative industries signal reputational and policy risk around generative AI.
insights.quote: recent awards became mired in scandal over entries allegedly written by AI

insights.claim: The episode frames AI as raising concerns about 'cognitive debt', the 'dearth' of the author, and the risks of anthropomorphising technology.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Cognitive debt is a emerging critique of AI-assisted work that may shape adoption attitudes.

insights.claim: The episode asks whether struggle is a necessary part of the writing process, implicitly questioning the value of AI that removes it.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Value attributed to human effort in creative work could limit demand for AI-generated content.

insights.claim: AI enthusiasts use the term 'human sandwich' for a workflow pattern, which the episode promises to explain.
insights.speaker: Prospect Magazine
insights.so_what: Track emerging AI-workflow jargon as a signal of how human oversight is being positioned.
